_doc: Street centreline paths and the visible travelled strips for the 1 July 1835 scene. The platted corridors are 80 ft (24.384 m) wide; the bare or thinly grassed track drawn inside one is narrower and explicitly conjectural. Paths are analytic extensions of the committed street-control module and the 1834 plats, not traces of modern pavement. A path is clipped wherever the heightfield is water, so a platted line never paints an invented ford across a branch of the river. Surface classes follow chicago_dpw_1891_streets: earth only on this date. South Water and Lake are the early principal graded/turnpiked routes; the fall-1836 work on Canal, western Lake, and Randolph is not backdated. The Gurdon Hubbard La Salle segment is omitted as a special improvement because his petition is dated twelve days after this scene. `path_local_enu_m` is the PLATTED line and it is what the plat, corridor and lot derivations read; a street may also carry `drawn_track_local_enu_m`, which is the worn wheel line the renderer paints and which those derivations ignore. The two are separate claims and one field cannot carry both — a bend added to the plat line moves platted lot lines the whole length of the street and re-scores the corridor-intrusion count (measured on T-0111, both gates red). A drawn track is checked at compile time to stay inside its own platted corridor and to overhang the platted line's ends by no more than 4 m, so it can meet a bridge abutment and cannot become an unplatted street.
surface_standard: No gravel or hard paving is shown. 'graded' and 'turnpiked' are rendered as drained or thrown-up earth with wagon wear; ordinary streets are worn native soil with a grassy crown and margins.

RE-FITTED OFF THE PLAT'S OWN MODULE FOR T-0827, 2026-09-12, and it is no longer fitted to N Wacker Drive. Until this reading the whole line was ONE modern junction and a bearing: its north vertex WAS `control.lake_market` — West Lake Street crossing North Upper Wacker Drive, read off OpenStreetMap — to the centimetre, and `refused_control.market_south_water` records the only other junction this project has looked for on this street and could not make. Wacker Drive was built in 1926 on ground made when the river was walled, so that one control stands on ground that did not exist in 1835. THE PITCH IS WHAT SETTLES IT, because Market's centre to Franklin's is one 400 ft module of the plat and three readings of it disagree with the committed lines in the same direction: the platted module is 121.92 m; the Wright 1834 sheet reads 120.21 m — five steps of the uniform ladder of block boundary lines its Lake Street traverse crosses east of the river, committed as pixels in data/traces/vectors/street_corridors_1834.json; the Thompson plat's North Division tier reads 124.81 m (T-0451). The two independently measured sheets BRACKET the module, 1.7 m under and 2.9 m over, which is what two hand-drawn sheets carrying 3-4.5 % paper stretch should do — and the committed pitch of 118.0-119.2 m lay outside that bracket at every northing of the run, the only pitch on this grid that did, where the other five South Division pitches read 121.8-123.6 m. So the line is stepped one module west of the committed `franklin`, which has a real crossing of two named surface roadways at `control.south_water_franklin` and reproduces from it to 0.03 m, and it takes Franklin's bearing with it. It moves 2.72 m west at the south end and 3.30 m west at Lake Street; the northing extent is untouched, because this ticket moves the line across and not along. MARKET IS THE ONE STREET ON THIS GRID NO SHEET FIXES DIRECTLY, and that is why the module had to do it: the street's west side is the river bank its whole length — which is why Wacker Drive stands there now — so the Wright traverse crosses 107 m of blank paper where this line runs, and the Thompson plat cuts block 21 off at the Wolf Point triangle before its west line, leaving its south tier with no measured Market face either. The derivation is tools/measure_market_line.py and its assertions are part of tools/check.sh. streets.drawn_track_note: The platted line stops at [699, 18], on the crest of the drawbridge approach fill, 2.70 m short of the causeway. The worn wheel line does not: it leaves the platted line at the South Water corner and runs one straight 13.8 m chord onto the fill's own axis, ending on the deck. RECONSTRUCTED, and what bounds it is measured. The last point IS the deck end — the south edge midpoint of the dearborn_street_drawbridge footprint, local E 697.65 / N 20.70, which is also line[0] of the dearborn_south approach in terrain_spec.json, so nothing here invents where the boards begin. The first point is the platted line at N 7.0, which is where south_water crosses it, so the swing starts at the corner the traffic comes from rather than at a chosen station. Held on the platted line the track's east edge would stand 4.87 m off the fill's axis, 0.87 m outside the 4.0 m half-width the earthwork is level across, and the last stride onto the causeway would be taken on a side slope; swung onto the axis, every metre of the 7 m width ends on the level crest. What is invented is that the swing is one chord and takes 13.8 m. ONE chord because the ribbon's panels are drawn square to their own chord and are not mitred at the joints, so each turn opens a wedge of prairie on the outside of it (3.5 tan(turn/2) wide at the ribbon's edge, nothing at its centre) and one 5.7-degree joint is the fewest and smallest a swing can be cut into: a 0.61 m2 sector, 0.17 m at its widest, inside the 0.84 m the road texture's own edge already fades out across — and because the joint stands at the corner, South Water Street's own 10.5 m roadway is drawn over half of it, so 0.30 m2 is what a 2 cm plan probe finds uncovered by any street. An eight-chord easement was measured first and was seven times worse (2.18 m2), because eight joints turn eight times. The line is never more than 1.37 m off the platted line, a ninth of the 80 ft corridor. See docs/LIBERTIES.md L178 and ticket T-0111.

streets.note: T-0445. THE WEST DIVISION'S RIVERFRONT STREET, SEATED OFF THE COMMITTED WATERLINE AND NOTHING ELSE. The plat carries five north-south streets west of the river — West Water, Canal, Clinton, Jefferson, Des Plaines (the owner's reading of the sheet, T-0443) — and this file held only the middle two. West Water is the one of the three missing lines the modelled ground can carry, so it is seated here and the other two are refused in docs/RESEARCH/west_division_streets.md with the measurement that refuses them. METHOD: the centreline is the committed west bank of the South Branch (data/terrain/epochs/e1834_harbor_cut/river.geojson, traced from Wright 1834 and graded inferred there) offset one half-corridor — 12.192 m — to the west, so the street's EAST KERB stands on the 1834 waterline. That is the furthest east an 80 ft street on this bank can be, which is the same bound T-0444's swap test rested on; taking the bound as the placement is this line's one reconstruction and WHAT WOULD MOVE IT IS STATED: any wharf or landing strip between the kerb and the water pushes the whole line west by its width, and no source reached gives that width. Every vertex is 12.19-12.29 m from the bank, so the kerb reaches the waterline and does not cross it. THE GRADE IS INHERITED and is not better than its anchor: the bank is inferred, so this is. THE REACH WAS CARRIED PAST THE TURN BY T-0768, AND IT STOPS WHERE A COMMITTED FOOTPRINT STANDS IN IT. T-0445 ended the line at local north -104, where the traced bank turns west into the junction pool at Wolf Point, because an offset line past the turn runs through the attested Wolf Point cluster; it did not measure how far past the turn the line gets FIRST, and the answer is 39.55 m. The same bank offset is carried along the bank's Wolf Point segment until the riverward corridor reaches JAMES KINZIE'S HOUSE, whose footprint spans 6.77-16.99 m west of the bank and therefore stands ACROSS the roadway rather than beside it, and the line is cut there: 37.12 m of new centreline, of which 20.30 m lies north of West Lake Street's north kerb. That is the frontage Fergus 1839's 'W. Water st north of West Lake st' attests and this reconstruction carried none of — the old end stood 6.79 m SOUTH of Lake's own north kerb, so the attested reach had zero length. JOINING THE TWO REACHES MITRES THE VERTEX AT THE TURN, which is why the old end [-9.34, -104.20] now reads [-7.92, -106.17]: it was the perpendicular end of the last segment and it is now the mitre joint between two, still 12.192 m from the bank. WHAT IS NOT SEATED, and the measurement that refuses it, is in docs/RESEARCH/west_division_streets.md § 1: past the cut five more committed placements — James Kinzie's house, Robert Kinzie's store, the Wolf Point tavern and its stable, the Robinson-Caldwell cabins and the Walker meeting house — stand 3.76-23.50 m from the traced bank at their nearest corners, so the widest clear strip between the water and the cluster is 3.76 m against the 24.384 m an 80 ft street needs, and no line fits riverward of them. ATTESTATION, all of it already committed here: Fergus 1839 prints three West Water addresses (a hotel at the Randolph corner, a grocery and ship stores near Randolph, the Rat's-castle Hotel north of West Lake) — 1839 evidence recalled in 1876, which attests the street and is NOT backdated into its 1835 wear, which is why the traffic grade here is the light one Clinton carries and not Canal's; and south_branch_raft_bridge's committed position puts its west landing on West Water Street, with the war-dance procession coming south along it. NOTHING SURVIVES ON THE LINE and the negative is recorded rather than passed over: an Overpass query for every named highway in the box 41.8825/-87.6395 to 41.8862/-87.6368, run 2026-09-05, returned Wacker Drive and its lower decks on the EAST bank, the cross streets, and the Riverwalk — no through street on the west bank of the South Branch. The bridge record's parenthetical gloss 'West Water Street (now Canal Street)' cannot be right for this line: the committed `canal` is fitted to modern Canal Street's own surviving intersections and stands 131-159 m west of it over the reach they share, which is about one plat module, exactly as the plat draws the two as separate streets.

The line uses the road-only Kinzie control already adopted by the North Branch bridge rather than the queued five-node bikeway-inclusive GCP. Its recorded turnpiking belongs to fall 1836 and is not backdated. ATTESTED FROM THE THOMPSON PLAT (T-0713, the owner's ruling of 2026-09-04). The fall-1836 grading work on Canal is still not backdated into this scene, which is a claim about surface and belongs to `surface_confidence`. WHICH READING, AND WHERE IT IS WRITTEN DOWN (T-0421, 2026-09-13). The sentence this note opens with — that the line uses the road-only Kinzie control — pointed at no record, and the coordinate it means lived in prose in three places. It is committed now as `data/traces/street_control.json` § control.kinzie_canal.road_only_reading (E 446891.71, N 4637657.80, the three road nodes of the five), and that entry names this record back. BOTH READINGS STAND, for stated reasons: the five-node mean stays the control point because it is georeferencing GCP HB and re-deriving it re-runs the Hathaway fit and re-bakes the North Branch bridge, and this line stays on the road-only reading because that is the one `node_rule` prescribes. WHAT THAT COSTS THIS STREET, now measured instead of asserted: `tools/plat_corridors.py` control_offsets() derives the platted corridor from the committed control, and against the five-node mean Canal's three control points spread 2.33 m (lake_canal +0.00, randolph_canal +0.09, kinzie_canal -2.24), which is `disagree` — no rigid translation satisfies all three, so Canal's corridor stays on this drawn line. Against `road_only_reading` the same three spread 0.09 m. The 2.33 m is the Kinzie Street Bikeway inside the control's average, not this street disagreeing with itself; the line reproduces its own control to 9 cm. NOTHING MOVES ON EITHER READING — 0.09 m is still wider than the 0.01 m the offsets are quoted to, so the verdict is `disagree` both ways and the corridor sits where it sat. `tools/measure_canal_control_spread.py` re-derives both numbers on every commit.

WHAT WOULD RAISE IT to `attested` is a second surviving intersection on this line, which would fit the bearing from control instead of inheriting it, the way Fulton's four do for its tier. The path spans local north -400.0 to +80.0, which is `clinton`'s own committed extent, because a line whose direction is borrowed from Clinton should not claim more ground than Clinton does. The plat rules this street further north and south; this reconstruction does not draw it further, and whatever extends Clinton extends this. THE GROUND IT STANDS ON, measured and not assumed. Sampled at 25 stations 20.0 m apart along the committed path, the heightfield reads 1.305 to 1.325 m above the 1835 water surface and not one station is at or below it (data/terrain/epochs/e1834_harbor_cut/heightfield.json, box local east -705.0..+1700.0). STATUS, argued rather than inherited. `track_width_m` is 0, `opened` and `worn` are false and the surface is `unworn_prairie` — the School Section grid's reading, carried here for the same reasons: nothing committed fronts this line, nothing reached attests traffic or wear on it, and the West Division beyond Canal Street was open ground in 1835 (Andreas: “The West Side was an open prairie, entirely free from timber”). AND ONE DISAGREEMENT THIS RECORD DOES NOT SETTLE: `jefferson_school_section`, the same street name south of Madison, runs due north-south at local east -379.98 on the School Section's own grid. Carried to Madison's northing this line would stand 8.3 m west of it. The two are different surveys and this file has always held them as different records; nothing here claims they met, and no line is bent to make them.

T-0446. THE ONE WEST DIVISION TIER THAT DOES NOT SURVIVE INSIDE THE PLAT, so its line is INTERPOLATED between two that do and is graded for that and nothing better. The plat carries the West Division's tiers north to south as Kinzie, Carroll, Fulton, Lake, Randolph, Washington (the owner's reading of the sheet, carried in T-0443); `kinzie` and the new `fulton` are both held by surviving intersection control, and Carroll is the single tier between them. MODERN CARROLL AVENUE IS NO USE HERE and the negative is recorded rather than passed over: an Overpass query for every way named Carroll between lon -87.68 and -87.632 on 2026-09-04 returned eight, and not one of them meets Canal, Clinton, Jefferson or Des Plaines. The two fragments nearest the plat are outside it in opposite directions - one at local north +193 to +199 and east -55 to +561, which is the Kinzie's Addition alignment on the far side of the North Branch, and one at north +95 to +133 more than 1,180 m west of the datum, in ground the Thompson plat never covered. Inside the original town Carroll was taken by the Union Station approaches and the Kennedy Expressway. METHOD: the centreline is the midpoint of `kinzie` and `fulton` at every easting, which is 139.16 at the west end T-1443 carried it to, 137.85 at the old east -320 clip and 136.47 at the bank. THE BRACKET IS STATED BECAUSE IT IS THE HONEST WIDTH OF THIS READING: the two tiers are not evenly spaced on the surviving grid - at local east -250 Kinzie to Fulton measures 250.30 m against Fulton to Lake's 119.91 m - so stepping one Fulton-to-Lake module south from Kinzie puts Carroll at north 142.63 and one module north from Fulton puts it at 132.16. The midpoint, 137.40 at that easting, sits between them and is 5.24 m from either, which is this line's uncertainty and is larger than any other West Division street's. tools/measure_west_division_tiers.py --self-test holds the midpoint inside that bracket, so a later re-derivation of kinzie or fulton cannot leave this line behind. THE EAST END IS THE WATER, not a bend: the path stops 3 m short of the committed west bank of the North Branch, because no source gives Carroll a crossing and the tier does not continue on the far side under this name in 1835. Track width and wear are visual interpretation, and the narrowest in this file, because no committed structure fronts this tier at all. WEST TO DES PLAINES STREET (T-1443). The line is carried 204.88 m west of the clip at local east -320 to [-524.877, 139.16], where it meets fulton's own west end — an interpolation claims no more ground than the pair it lies between. The clip was this reconstruction's own extent and never a claim that the street ended there; T-1416 built the modelled field out to local east -705 and T-1430 seated the street it now stops at, so the two reasons it stood are both gone. THE REACH IS CARRIED FROM THE OLD WEST END, NOT FITTED THROUGH IT: the bearing is -0.006394, read from carroll's own westernmost committed segment, [-320, 137.85] to [-104.96, 136.47]. Every committed vertex east of -320 is left exactly where it stood — the old west end is KEPT as a vertex rather than replaced — so no platted lot line moves, no corridor is re-cut and the corridor-intrusion count is untouched. What the carry does add is a 0.0013 deg change of direction AT that retained vertex, and it is stated here rather than rounded away. The confidence is unchanged, because carrying a line the length the sheet already drew it is not an upgrade. THE GROUND IS MEASURED: 42 samples along the new reach against the committed heightfield, none off the modelled box, the lowest standing 1.215 m above the summer-1835 water surface. THE RULE IS UNCHANGED AND THE DATUM MOVES WITH IT: west of the clip the Kinzie term is `kinzie_west`, T-1085's separate record, because that is the line that exists there. At the west end the midpoint is 139.16 and the bracket is 132.624 (one Fulton-to-Lake module north of Fulton) to 145.696 (one module south of Kinzie), so the half-bracket — this line's uncertainty, and still the largest in the file — is 6.536 m. Carroll stops at Fulton's west end and no further: an interpolation may claim no more ground than the pair it lies between.

DERIVED FROM THE COMMITTED NORTH BANK by tools/derive_north_water.py, not drawn beside it. The line this replaced was a hand-drawn schematic that ran 477.4 m of its 843.3 m INSIDE the terrain's water mask, so the renderer drew no roadway at all across that reach and three of its six bends stood in the river (T-0226). The bank is a trace of Wright 1834 with a stated +/-20 m; this line was not a trace of anything and said so; the old line missed the bank by 1 to 86 m, up to 4.3x that uncertainty; and the North Division placement recipe had already ruled that proximity to North Water Street never overrides the water mask. So the street was the record that was wrong. North Water Street fronted the main stem, so its platted corridor is laid with its south line on the bank and the centreline half a platted street clear of it - 12.192 m, half the 80 ft thompson_module_1830. THAT HALF MODULE IS A DISTANCE, so the requirement at each 5 m station is the bank's OFFSET CURVE: the northern boundary of the traced bank dilated by a 12.192 m disc, which is the locus of points exactly half a street from the bank whatever bearing the bank runs at. It is fitted in the fewest straight runs that clear every station with 0.5 m of give, which is 2.5 % of the bank trace's own uncertainty. Until T-0307 the requirement was instead the bank's running maximum over +/-15 m of easting plus a NORTHWARD setback, and both halves of that assume an east-west bank; see WHAT THE WEST REACH COSTS, stated because the tool measures it (T-0307, which re-derived it). Coming round Wolf Point into the forks the bank falls 45 m of northing in 35 m of easting. Under the old rule a running maximum taken 15 m ahead of a bank that steep added most of that drop to the setback, and a northward offset bought only its cosine back, so the road stood up to 41.5 m from the water on the tool's own northward-ray reading - three and a half street widths where a half module is 12.2. The offset curve states the intended thing at any bearing and the verge came in. Measured as nearest water in any direction, which is the honest perpendicular distance and is also new in T-0307: west of the slough 5.50 m .. 25.50 m before, 5.50 m .. 20.00 m after; east of the slough 9.50 m .. 25.50 m before, 8.50 m .. 20.50 m after; the dry climb to Kinzie unmoved at 12.00 m .. 27.00 m. The line went from 19 authored bends to 24, which is the cost of following a bank instead of a lookahead. THE TWO TIGHT SPOTS ARE RULED ON, NOT TUNED - T-0372, and neither vertex moved. The 5.50 m is the street's own west terminus at [-30, 45.2] and the 8.50 m is the slough crossing's east abutment, and the ruling is that BOTH are places where this street meets water on purpose: it ends AT the fork, where the street ended, and it arrives AT a bridgehead, which T-0254 already required of it. The two alternatives were refused with numbers rather than by preference. Raising the requirement onto the water mask - nearest water in any direction, which would see the North Branch and the bay as well as the main stem - cannot be met at a crossing at all: to stand a half module off the water at the deck's east end this street would have to be 25.5 m north of the deck at E +196 and 15.0 m north at E +200, with the deck at N +157.5, which is a street that never reaches the bridge. Retreating the terminus east until the branch is a half module off costs 11.0 m of centreline and ends the street at E -20, where there is no feature to end at; it buys 6.7 m of clearance by making the terminus arbitrary instead of sourced. So the exemption is written down and BOUNDED, and the rest of the street is gated on the half module rather than the whole line being loosened to five metres - a flat 5 m rule would stop testing the 97 per cent of this street where the half module is the actual requirement. tools/derive_north_water.py --gate now enforces two tiers and refuses either: the OPEN REACH owes 11.5 m, the half module less the fit's own 0.5 m of give, and measures 12.00 m today over 571 probes; THE WEST TERMINUS (the last 10 m to the branch) and THE CROSSING'S APPROACHES (10 m either side of the deck) owe 5 m, and measure 5.50 m and 8.50 m over 16 probes - 32 m of the street's 1175.8 m. The open reach carries only 0.5 m of margin, which is deliberate: this gate is here to refuse drift toward the water, so a bank that moves under the street should turn it red and be re-derived rather than absorbed. --self-test proves all three tiers refuse a line walked toward the water, and that 13 committed probes at the two ends are under the open reach's floor - the exemptions are what hold this line up, not decoration. Geometry stays reconstructed - a bank is a proxy for a street, not evidence of one, and west of the slough there is not even a building on it. Track width and wear remain visual interpretation.

READ OFF THE THOMPSON PLAT FOR T-0451, 2026-09-05, and seated on the committed line it continues. The sheet held at chicago/pre_fire_v1/maps/images/1830_thompson_plat.png draws ONE tier of blocks in the North Division, numbered 1 at the Due North line and 7 at the North Branch, with six 80 ft corridors between them; this record is the corridor between blocks 7 and 6. THE PLAT LETTERS NO NAME IN ANY OF THEM — each carries the figure 80 at its head on the Kinzie line and a vertical ST. between the lot rows, and nothing else. The name here is the sheet's own lettering on the SAME LINE south of the river, where it writes MARKET in the Randolph-Washington tier, carried north because the sheet draws one line and not two. That is a carry and not a North Division reading, and `wolcott` — the one North Division line this project already held — is the standing proof that a name on this side of the river could differ. THE LINE ITSELF is the committed `market` centreline extended north from North Water Street to Kinzie Street, unbent: no vertex is invented and the bearing is the parent's. What the plat independently says about it is the check, not the source — measured by tools/measure_north_division_streets.py off data/traces/thompson_north_division_streets.json, the corridor's centre on the sheet stands -9.08 m from this line at the tier's own northing, and the corridor's centre north of the river stands -7.34 px from the same street's corridor south of it. The whole tier's block pitch is the South Division's own to 0.6 m in the mean. Every metre of the run stands on modelled ground the heightfield holds above water. THE PARENT LINE MOVED UNDER THIS RECORD, AND THIS RECORD MOVED WITH IT (T-0827, 2026-09-12). Until then market was the one of the six graded no better than `inferred`, and the number was why: the plat's corridor stood 9.08 m west of the line, four times the worst of the other five, and the committed market->franklin pitch of 118.0-119.2 m was the one South Division pitch off the plat's 400 ft module. The suspect was named in this record as the parent rather than the North Division, and that is how it read: `market` was fitted to modern N Wacker Drive, which stands on made ground. T-0827 re-fitted it off the module — Franklin stepped one module west, bracketed by the Wright sheet's 120.21 m and this plat's own 124.81 m, with the committed pitch outside that bracket — and this line is the re-fitted parent extended north, still unbent and still on the parent's bearing. The plat's corridor now stands -5.19 m from it at the tier's own northing, which is still the worst of the six and is stated rather than smoothed: the other five read -0.26 to -2.29 m. That residual is COORDINATE UNCERTAINTY inside the datum's own 17.5 m, not a doubt about a street the sheet draws, so on T-0713's ruling this line now carries the plat's attestation with the other five. `name_2026` is null here for the same reason: N Wacker Drive north of the river is the east-west riverside drive and is not this line, and no modern name was established for it. THE SOUTH END is also the least settled of the six: it lands on `north_water`'s committed centreline at the reach T-0447 has open, where the plat does not give North Water Street the ground it runs on. THE ROAD THE FORT PLAINLY HAD, DRAWN AT THE RECONSTRUCTED TIER, and which part is which is stated rather than implied. WHAT IS DOCUMENTED: the fort had large gates north and south - Juliette Kinzie inside it in 1831, Andreas independently, and a break in each of those two walls and in neither of the others on the 1830 Harrison plan - and the garrison garden's own record reads off that same plan that the plot lies 'west of the road'. So the plan draws a road on the reservation, and a road that is east of that garden and arrives at that gate has to run about here. WHAT IS NOT DOCUMENTED: nobody traced this line, nobody measured it, and no source names it. The 1835 name is DESCRIPTIVE, not a proper name; the 2026 name is the street that runs over this ground today, not a descent of name. THE WESTERN REACH IS THE INVENTION AND IT IS THE REASON THIS RECORD IS RECONSTRUCTED: South Water Street stops at the United States Reservation, matching the 1833 order, so the connection from the town to the fort gate was never a platted street - it is drawn because a garrisoned post that mustered, traded and drew its stores through the town had a way in, and a visitor who walks east out of South Water Street should find one instead of trackless prairie. The line is routed clear of the garden's east corner and of the Beaubien buildings, and it is clipped by the water mask like every other track, so it makes honest gaps rather than fords where the ground is wet. Recorded in docs/LIBERTIES.md; T-0044.

BOTH ENDS ARE DERIVED FROM COMMITTED RECORDS AND THE MIDDLE IS ONE STRAIGHT CHORD. It begins at [1156.63, 253.92]: the north gate's own centre — 26.5 m along a 53 m wall, the midpoint tools/measure_fort_gates.py reads the shipped leaves at — carried out along the wall's outward normal by 6.74 m, which is the standoff the fort road already keeps from the SOUTH gate. The apron's bare trodden earth carries the last stride to the pickets at both gates, and this record invents no second convention for the north one. It ends at [1133.40, 259.61]: the Z = 0 waterline of the committed heightfield, on the easting of the WEST END of the commandant's quarters — the one place on this bank any source puts anything, the 1855 Hesler key locating the ferry landing 'under the west chimney of the Commandant's quarters'. READ THE DATE: that key is 1855 and describes the post-military compound, so it is read here as an inference that a landing fixed by the shape of a bank stood where it stood twenty years earlier, and never as a measurement of 1835. WHY ONE OBLIQUE CHORD AND NOT A RAMP STRAIGHT DOWN. Straight north out of the gate the graded bank falls 3.60 m in under 10 m, about 1 in 2.7, which is a scramble rather than a way to a boat. Swung west onto the landing the same fall is spread over 23.91 m: 1 in 6.65 mean and 1 in 3.65 at its steepest metre, measured on the committed heightfield at [1140.0, 257.99]. That worst metre is GENTLER THAN GROUND THIS PROJECT ALREADY DRAWS ROADWAY ON — South Water Street reaches 1 in 3.0 at the river bank, Randolph and Washington 1 in 4.1 — so the obliquity is what makes the track walkable and is not a shape chosen for its own sake. One chord means no joint, so no wedge of prairie opens at a bend (L178). The width is the GATE'S: 3.60 m, the committed gate_width_m of the palisade this track leaves by, rather than a fourth invented figure on this reservation. The corridor is the fort road's 12.0 m for the same reason. Clipped by the water mask like every other track, so the ribbon stops at the water instead of painting a ford. Madison Street, the section's own north line and the boundary of the Town of Chicago. Read off Wright's 1834 survey as a ruled line of the School Section's grid (Section 16, T39N R14E) and anchored on the section's own mile square; the measured line is at local N -546.0 m and the anchor moves it +26.9 m. THE STATUS IS THE OWNER'S READING OF THE SHEET, 2026-09-05: 'no alleys and no street names but still a grid that should have some wilderness trees'. So the corridor is platted and the ground inside it is not: `track_width_m` is 0 because no wagon track is drawn or attested here, `alleys` is false because the sheet rules none inside these blocks, and the flora belts are not cut for it. What a visitor should see is a survey line over prairie, not a road. DRAWN LEVEL, AND THAT IS A STATEMENT ABOUT THE GROUND RATHER THAN THE PAPER (T-0959). Re-measured off the same registered raster in ten bands along its length, this line does NOT run level: all thirteen east-west lines of the section tilt the same way, median 0.57 degrees, 16.0 m of rise across the mile. That settles nothing on its own, because all fourteen NORTH-SOUTH lines tilt the same way too, median 0.67 degrees, and a rotation of the drawing under its registration tilts the two families equally and OPPOSITELY. What settles it is the section's own boundary. Section 16's four sides are PLSS lines and run true north and true east on the ground by definition; measured exactly as the interior lines are, they tilt +0.69 degrees in this frame against +0.56 for the interior. A frame that tilts its own cardinal control is describing itself, and the mechanism is in the fit: a general affine with two axis scales 6.2 per cent apart does not preserve angles, so a right angle ruled on the paper leaves it at 91.62 degrees. The tilt therefore comes out with the rest of the registration's distortion when the measured lines are rescaled onto the section's statute-mile square — the same anchoring that removes the 3 per cent north-south overrun. `geometry_confidence` stays `inferred` for that reason: the northing is a measurement carried onto a PLSS square, not a figure any record states.
